newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama pays U.S. invasion victims $1.67 million.
newsitem.headline: Panama pays U.S. invasion victims $1.67 million.

text.p: The Panamanian government doled out $1.67 million on Thursday to nearly 3,500 families who lost relatives and homes during the December 1989 U.S. invasion, a top government official said.
Some 25,000 U.S. troops invaded and later captured strongman Manuel Antonio Noriega, now serving a 40-year prison sentence in Florida for a 1992 conviction on drug and racketeering charges.

"This was a promise made by the government of President Ernesto Perez Balladares to pay the families nearly $12 million," deputy Housing Minister Rogelio Paredes Robles said. "The amount of damage is incalculable. It's a way to reimburse those humble Panamanians who did not ask for the invasion," he told Reuters.

The families, from the working class neighbourhood of El Chorrillo which was razed by bombs the night of the Dec. 20 attack, will get another $9 million in staggered payments until 1999. The funds come from a tax on slot machines from Panama's 20 casinos.

Robles said Panama filed several lawsuits with international human rights organisations to get the United States to pay. "But we never got anywhere. The U.S. government maintains it was a time of war and they don't owe any retributions," he said.
Government officials estimate at least 5,000 Panamanians were killed and billions of dollars were lost during the invasion.
In December 1990, following the invasion, officials of the U.S. southern command and Panamanian officials said 202 Panamanian civilians were killed.

According to the U.S. Defence Department, 23 U.S. troops were killed in action and 314 wounded. Two other American troops died but not in the fighting. Three American civilians were killed in the fighting.
A total of 314 Panamanian troops were killed and 124 were wounded, according to the Pentagon.
